requirements.requirement: /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 is treated as the authoritative source
requirements.summary: No app.conf existed on node1 initially; executor created it as the source file, and all subsequent syncs fetch from node1 and push to node2 (never the reverse). Confirmed by cmd-3ee7024bf7d84859 (absence check) and cmd-56586f8110934bdd (creation with checksum dad0f1567f3fb07758022a20a63d868a).

requirements.requirement: node2's copy stays synchronized with node1, picking up any change within 15 minutes
requirements.summary: A 5-minute cron job on node3 runs the Ansible playbook to fetch node1's app.conf and copy it to node2 (well inside the 15-minute SLA). Multiple independent content changes on node1 (max_connections 50->75->90->123, each with a distinct checksum) were observed to propagate to node2 automatically via the scheduled cron tick (not manual triggers) within a few minutes each time, both before and after a full restart cycle of all three nodes.

requirements.requirement: Synchronization must be implemented using Ansible
requirements.summary: node3 (the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed) was used as control node. An inventory (hosts.ini) and playbook (sync-playbook.yml, using ansible.builtin.fetch and ansible.builtin.copy) were authored and invoked both manually and via cron-driven run-sync.sh, with successful play recaps showing changed=true on the copy task.

requirements.requirement: Independent requirement: run the node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node with pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id/service/checksum captured for all three nodes (cmd-b174b5188b364ced, cmd-913fde4bf9aa4fa1, cmd-21aef92164ab47f1), matching the fixed before_prepare snapshot values. Each node was rebooted individually with an acknowledgement, an observed unreachable window, and a distinct post-restart boot_id matching the fixed after_executor snapshot (node1: 1e0cb179...->3a83264a...; node2: 901ef286...->14de4c7d...; node3: 6fd57414...->65e902c2...). Post-restart recovery was verified: ssh active and app.conf checksum intact on node1/node2, cron active with crontab and sync files intact on node3. The sync pipeline was further validated end-to-end after node3's own restart by pushing a new node1 change and confirming automatic cron-driven propagation.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material contract outcomes: node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf was established and treated as the source of truth, and an Ansible-based mechanism (playbook + 5-minute cron on the control node) reliably propagates content changes to node2 well within the 15-minute SLA, demonstrated across multiple change cycles both before and after a full restart of all three nodes. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for all three nodes, with baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were identified; the one failed SSH-service start was a diagnosed and corrected prerequisite rather than an unrelated experiment.
limitations: The 120-second proxy timeout on cmd-79882a24a8e642f8 interrupted one polling attempt during the 15-minute sync demonstration; the immediately following command (cmd-2c97d780014649f9) still confirmed the sync log and final checksum, so this does not weaken the finding but is noted for completeness.

Evidence for the sync mechanism relies on md5 checksum matches and Ansible play recaps rather than direct byte-for-byte diffs of file content in every cycle, though the checksums plus periodic full cat outputs are consistent and mutually corroborating.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 58 timeline commands chronologically. State-changing actions fall into clear categories, each tied to a material purpose: (1) enabling sshd and generating host keys on node1/node2 (cmd-97f7d98a806f4631, cmd-45c18c85c97540e2 failed due to missing keys, immediately diagnosed via cmd-837c35a6cf374c5c and corrected by cmd-eb709faf7695461a/cmd-df5f6aead39f47b9 -- a legitimate corrective sequence, not an abandoned experiment); (2) authorizing node3's SSH key and creating /etc/inventory + the source-of-truth app.conf on node1/node2 (cmd-56586f8110934bdd, cmd-697090ccd59a4a47), required for the task; (3) building the Ansible inventory, playbook, sync script, and cron job on node3 (cmd-c840200f33184ae2, cmd-074fc33ebd284c63, cmd-7fae7b47ca554ad6), required for the task; (4) the mandated node restarts (cmd-e93c54d5ac014140, cmd-3b137affca5e424f, cmd-70100b1ea9154878). No unnecessary or abandoned mutations, conflicting services, unsafe new exposure, or damaged package state were found; the /tmp systemd-private directories that differ pre/post are OS-generated reboot artifacts, not executor residue. The one failed ssh.service start was a diagnosed and promptly corrected prerequisite step rather than an unrelated experiment.
